message.content:
Work in /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TS, LIVE prod tree). You OWN visitor-analytics: the tracking/aggregation layer + a NEW admin analytics dashboard page. Do NOT edit the sidebar/nav (report your new route; I wire the nav), chrome, mail, or chat.

Two Nxeon-board cards:
- cmst3gdnl "Breakdown of visitors": the owner is running ads and wants an average breakdown of website visitors — what people do on the site, how long they stay, and the funnel toward sign-up/deploy.
- cmst3swqt "Better Analytics": more data/analytics, and specifically **recurring visitors**.

First map what already exists: lib/tracking.ts, the Visit model + VisitTracker component, MetricsDaily, HealthSample, any GA4 wiring, and the internal /api/track beacon. Then:
1. Ensure/extend server-side capture of: pageviews per path, session duration (time on site), entry/exit, referrer/UTM, and a stable visitor id so RECURRING vs new visitors can be distinguished (respect the existing consent model).
2. Aggregate into daily/rolling metrics (extend MetricsDaily or add a lightweight table if needed — ADDITIVE Prisma changes only, new models/fields, never alter existing).
3. Build an ADMIN analytics dashboard page (new route under app/admin/…) showing: visitors (new vs recurring), avg time on site, top pages, referrers/UTM sources, and a signup→deploy funnel. Server-render from the aggregates; keep it fast.

Constraints: NO `npm run build`/`next build` — `npx tsc --noEmit` only. Prisma changes ADDITIVE only. Report: what tracking existed vs what you added, the new route, any new Prisma models/fields (so I can db push), tsc result.

model Visit {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  ip        String
  path      String
  referrer  String?
  ua        String?
  kind      String   @default("marketing") // marketing | portal
  userId    String?
  country   String?
  region    String?
  city      String?
  lat       Float?
  lng       Float?
  geocoded  Boolean  @default(false)
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([createdAt])
  @@index([ip])
}

// ---- Geo cache (IP -> location), populated best-effort by the worker ----
model GeoCache {
  ip        String   @id
  country   String?
  region    String?
  city      String?
  lat       Float?
  lng       Float?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
}

// ---- Teams / organizations ----
model Organization {
  id        String       @id @default(cuid())
  name      String
  ownerId   String
  owner     User         @relation("OrgOwner", fields: [ownerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  members   Membership[]
  createdAt DateTime     @default(now())
}

model Membership {
  id        String       @id @default(cuid())
  orgId     String
  org       Organization @relation(fields: [orgId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  userId    String
  user      User         @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  role      String       @default("MEMBER") // OWNER | ADMIN | MEMBER | BILLING
  areas     Json? // per-member allowed dashboard areas (null = role default); string[] of area keys
  createdAt DateTime     @default(now())

  @@unique([orgId, userId])
}

// ---- Gift / credit codes ----
model GiftCode {
model HealthSample {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  component String // web | proxmox | worker | db
  status    String // operational | degraded | down
  latencyMs Int?
  detail    String?
  ts        DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([component, ts])
  @@index([ts])
}

/// An incident on the public status page — auto-opened when a component stays
/// unhealthy across sweeps, or posted by an operator. Gives the status page a
/// real incident history and per-incident timeline.
model StatusIncident {
  id         String    @id @default(cuid())
  component  String? // affected component, or null for platform-wide
  severity   String    @default("degraded") // degraded | down | maintenance
  title      String
  body       String    @default("")
  startedAt  DateTime  @default(now())
  resolvedAt DateTime?
  auto       Boolean   @default(false) // opened automatically vs by an operator
  createdAt  DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt  DateTime  @updatedAt

  @@index([startedAt])
  @@index([resolvedAt])
}

/// Company mailboxes on the Nxeon domain (admin@, support@, santino@, …).
/// Provisioned on Mailcow and managed from the admin portal, FREE — deliberately
/// NOT tied to the customer EmailSubscription/EmailPlan/billing model, so they
/// never touch a wallet, plan limit, or subscription. Purely a company resource.
model CompanyMailbox {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  address     String   @unique // full email, e.g. admin@nxeon.cloud
  label       String? // optional friendly label (e.g. "Support desk")
  passwordEnc String // AES-256-GCM (lib/crypto-box) — the Mailcow mailbox password
  quotaMB     Int      @default(2048)
  status      String   @default("ACTIVE") // ACTIVE | FAILED
  createdById String? // admin who created it (audit only; nullable)
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())

  // Per-mailbox settings — mirror of the Mailbox columns, so staff-resolved
  // company mailboxes (resolveMailbox → id "company:<id>") persist identity,
  // signature, auto-reply and forwarding the same way customer mailboxes do.
  // Without these, saveMailboxSettings/saveForwarding/saveAutoReply threw P2025.
  displayName        String?
  replyTo            String?
  organization       String?
model MetricsDaily {
  id              String       @id @default(cuid())
  date            DateTime // UTC day
  scope           MetricsScope
  scopeId         String
  sent            Int          @default(0)
  delivered       Int          @default(0)
  hardBounce      Int          @default(0)

I also need to capture UTM params and referrer, plus figure out how to measure time on site — likely via a beacon on page unload or visibility change that reports dwell time. For the schema, I'm thinking through whether adding new optional fields to an existing model counts as "altering" it versus being purely additive, since the instructions say new models/fields are fine but existing structures shouldn't be changed.

I'm settling on adding nullable fields to the Visit model: visitorId, sessionId, utmSource, utmMedium, utmCampaign, durationMs, and an isEntry boolean flag to mark the first pageview of a session — all safe, additive, and non-destructive for a db push.

To fill durationMs, I'm planning a per-pageview id generated client-side that gets sent on the initial track call, then a follow-up "duration" beacon fired on navigation, visibility change, or pagehide that updates that same row via the pageview id, so the track endpoint needs to support both create and update actions.

Each pageview POST closes out the prior page's dwell time, with a pagehide beacon closing the final page — so the server just updates the Visit record matching the closed pvid with its duration. Summing per-page dwell gives session duration, and entry/exit pages can be derived from session state (first pageview = entry, last = exit), though I'm considering just adding an explicit flag to make this simpler at query time.

I'm weighing whether to build a separate daily rollup table for fast dashboard queries, but computing new-vs-recurring visitors per day requires knowing prior-day first-seen status, which adds real complexity. Given the business is early-stage with low traffic volume, I'm leaning toward skipping the heavy aggregation table and just querying the raw Visit data directly since the dataset is still small enough to be fast.

Given the real constraints, the cleanest approach is to extend Visit with additive fields like visitorId, sessionId, UTM params, pvid, duration, and entry flag, then update /api/track to manage the visitor cookie, capture session/UTM data, and handle duration beacons. For reliably capturing dwell time, I'm weighing pagehide versus visibilitychange — tab switches shouldn't prematurely close out a pageview, so I want to rely on pagehide for actual navigation/unload events combined with explicit close signals on SPA route changes, using sendBeacon when available and falling back to fetch with keepalive. Everything is complete and validated. Note: the `git diff --stat` shows many files I did not touch — those are pre-existing uncommitted WIP from other sessions in this live tree; I left them alone. My work is confined to the tracking/analytics layer.

## Summary

I own the visitor-analytics layer. Here's what I found already in place versus what I added.

### What tracking already existed
- **`Visit` model** — one row per pageview: `ip, path, referrer, ua, kind, userId, geo…, createdAt`.
- **`components/VisitTracker.tsx`** — client beacon firing `POST /api/track` on SPA route changes (30s dedupe), mounted in `app/(marketing)/layout.tsx` and `components/portal/Shell.tsx`.
- **`/api/track`** — bot-filtered, IP-rate-limited insert of a `Visit` row using the proxy-attested IP.
- **`lib/analytics.ts`** — read-only aggregations: views, unique-by-IP, referrers, countries/cities, recent/feed, globe.
- **`/admin/visitors`** — live traffic + geo dashboard. **`/admin/analytics`** — business (revenue/plans), *not* visitor behaviour.
- Consent model in **`lib/consent.ts`** — cookie `nxeon_cookie_consent` = `all|necessary|null`, default-on/opt-out (`marketingAllowed()` = not "necessary").
- **Gaps:** no session/time-on-site, no entry/exit, no UTM, no stable visitor id (recurring was IP-only), no visitor daily rollup, no behaviour/funnel dashboard. Note: `lib/tracking.ts` is ads-conversion (Meta CAPI/GA4), unrelated to visitor capture.

### What I added
1. **Capture (`VisitTracker.tsx` + `/api/track`)** — per-tab `sessionId` (30-min idle window), per-pageview `pvid`, `isEntry` landing flag, `utm_source/medium/campaign` (parsed from the landing URL, remembered for the session), and dwell-time **close beacons** (`navigator.sendBeacon` on pagehide/visibility-hidden + on SPA nav) that stamp `durationMs` onto the pageview. A **stable, consent-gated `visitorId`** is minted server-side as an httpOnly `nx_vid` cookie — only when consent ≠ `"necessary"`; opted-out visitors stay `visitorId=null` and are counted by IP only. Rate limit raised 60→120/min to absorb close beacons.
2. **Aggregation (`lib/analytics.ts`, additive)** — `newVsRecurring`, `visitorTimeStats` (avg time on site / pages-per-session / bounce), `topPages`, `topEntryPages`, `topUtmSources`, `topUtmCampaigns`, `signupDeployFunnel`, `computeVisitorDay`, `readVisitorDailySeries`. Plus **`worker/analytics.ts` → `visitorRollupSweep()`** wired into the worker loop (~15 min) rolling the last 3 UTC days into `VisitorDaily`.
3. **New admin page — route `app/admin/audience/page.tsx` (`/admin/audience`)** — server-rendered, `requireArea("analytics")`, `?days=7|30|90`. Shows: unique visitors + recurring share, avg time on site, bounce rate; a 30-day pageviews/unique-visitors trend (reads `VisitorDaily`, overlays a live "today"); new-vs-recurring donut; the **Visitors → Signups → Deployed → Paid funnel** with step conversions; and ranked top UTM sources/campaigns, referrers, top pages, and landing pages.

### New Prisma (additive only — needs `db push`)
- **`Visit`**: new nullable/defaulted fields `visitorId, sessionId, pvid, durationMs, isEntry(@default false), utmSource, utmMedium, utmCampaign` + indexes on `visitorId, sessionId, pvid`. No existing field altered.
- **New model `VisitorDaily`**: `date(@unique), pageviews, sessions, uniqueVisitors, newVisitors, returningVisitors, bounces, totalSessionMs(BigInt), signups, deployed`.

### Action needed / notes
- **Run `npx prisma db push`** before this code goes live — the new columns/table must exist or `Visit.create` with the new fields will error. I already ran `npx prisma generate` in the tree so tsc resolves.
- **Wire the nav** yourself: add a link to `/admin/audience` (and optionally map it to the `"analytics"` area in `lib/rbac.ts` `HREF_AREA`; the page already self-gates via `requireArea("analytics")`, ADMIN-only).
- **tsc result:** `npx tsc --noEmit` → exit 0 (clean); `npx prisma validate` → valid.
